narrative.overview: A late-evening data desk: a dark, quiet room where the only lit object is the curve. A calm, exact record of who is buying U.S. government debt, for a curious reader who is not a trader. Everything that is not data recedes; colour is spent on the heatmap and charts, where it carries meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only. One theme, no toggle and no light fallback.
Colour belongs to the data: a fixed ±3σ red↔blue scale, with lightness also carrying the signal.
Flat and ruled: tonal surfaces plus 1px rules; shadow only on floating tooltips.
Numbers in monospace, claims in serif, explanations in sans.
Honest states: stale, loading, empty and failed are each drawn plainly, never hidden.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Red and blue appear only on data marks. Never use them for buttons, links, borders or decoration.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: The scale is clamped at ±3σ and never auto-fitted, so a shade means the same thing permanently. Beyond-scale values keep the endpoint colour and get a dark dot.

rules.name: The Lightness-Carries-Signal Rule
rules.body: On the dark scale lightness rises with |value|, so the chart still reads in greyscale. Direction in greyscale comes from position against the legend.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader might compare is set in IBM Plex Mono.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest. Shadows appear only on elements that float above the page.

dos: Do keep red and blue exclusively for data marks and the legend.
Do keep the scale clamped at ±3σ and mark beyond-scale values with a dark dot (cells) or a triangle (charts).
Do set every comparable number in IBM Plex Mono.
Do keep body and muted text at 4.5:1 or better on Night Desk and Ledger Panel.
Do give every heatmap cell tenor, month and value as accessible text, and never let colour be the only encoding.
Do state stale, loading, empty and failed states in words.
Do place each metric's plain-language explanation beside it.
donts: Don't add a light theme, a theme toggle, or a light-coloured surface.
Don't use red or blue for buttons, links, borders or any non-data decoration.
Don't add drop shadows to cards or panels; only floating tooltips may cast one.
Don't auto-fit the colour scale to the data.
Don't call bid dispersion a "tail", or imply bid-to-cover is the headline measure.
Don't use side-stripe borders, gradient text, or decorative glows.
